p: A Thursday browse is a great excuse to find out a bit more about this proud little town. Bedlington has deep roots in coal mining and heavy industry, and it played a surprisingly important part in the early railway age. Bedlington Ironworks, which stood beside the River Blyth, produced wrought-iron rails in the early 1800s that helped show the way forward for railways, and George Stephenson used rails made here. It's the kind of local history that makes a wander round town feel all the more interesting.

For a dose of fresh air, Plessey Woods Country Park sits just a few miles away near Hartford Bridge, with woodland trails, a river and a meadow that's lovely for a picnic or a family walk. Humford Mill, on the River Blyth on the edge of town, is another pleasant green spot for a riverside stroll. The town's Front Street has plenty of benches and green space too, ideal for a rest with a cuppa after your browse.

A short drive east brings you to the coast at Blyth, where you'll find a long sandy beach, colourful beach huts and a busy harbour. Further north, Druridge Bay offers miles of quieter dunes and sand. A morning at the market followed by an afternoon by the sea makes for a cracking, low-cost day out in this corner of Northumberland. If you're travelling in by public transport, the Northumberland Line has been bringing passenger trains back to this part of the county, so it's worth seeing whether it suits your journey. It's a corner of the county that's easy to overlook and well worth a slower look.
